description: Accessible, themable UI components built with Lit as standard custom elements. They work in any web framework or with no framework.
rules: Import the component classes from the igniteui-webcomponents package root and register them with defineComponents(), for example defineComponents(IgcButtonComponent). defineAllComponents() registers all components but makes the bundle larger.

Load one theme style sheet, for example igniteui-webcomponents/themes/light/bootstrap.css. The themes are material, bootstrap, indigo and fluent, each in light and dark. To change the theme at run time, call configureTheme('material', 'dark').

Tag names start with igc-, class names have the form Igc<Name>Component, and event names start with igc, for example igcChange. The Igc<Name>ComponentEventMap type gives the detail type of each event.
Set a property that has no attribute, such as an array or an object, in JavaScript. Only properties with an attribute can be set in HTML.
Form controls are form-associated custom elements. They submit their value with a form and support the Constraint Validation API, as native controls do.
Style a component through its CSS parts (::part()) and its CSS custom properties. Page selectors do not reach inside its shadow root.
In React, use the igniteui-react package, which wraps these components as React components with the Igr prefix, for example IgrButton.
In Angular, add CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA to the schemas of each standalone component or NgModule that uses igc- tags.
In Vue, set compilerOptions.isCustomElement to tag => tag.startsWith('igc-'), so that Vue does not resolve igc- tags as Vue components.

The charts are in igniteui-webcomponents-charts, the data grids in igniteui-webcomponents-grids and igniteui-grid-lite, and the dock manager in igniteui-dockmanager. They are not in igniteui-webcomponents.
